subject: Pen test coverage & remediation status — clarification on Hosted / Dedicated / Private scope
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: penetration test report + scope clarification for Redwood services

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this — Acme's security team is updating our third-party risk assessment. We reviewed Redwood's SOC 2 and the pen test summary on the security portal, but we need two clarifications before we can close our questionnaire items:

1) Coverage: Does the pen test and the 2025 exec summary provided to customers cover Hosted (Redwood-hosted API), Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated/reserved capacity), or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments? We need an explicit mapping of what environments were in scope.

2) Remediation status: For any findings classified as "high" or "critical", would you share the remediation status and dates? A simple tracker or CSV is fine.

Attached is our formal evidence request PDF with the fields we need. If some items are restricted, please state that and point us to the entitlement/process to request them (e.g., NDA, ATO).

Can we get a response by EOD next Tuesday (2026-03-16)?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

-Rajesh
Rajesh Patel
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

Attachment: ACME_PenTest_Request_2026-03.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope clarification for Redwood services

Hi Rajesh — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. Quick answers up front, followed by specifics:

- Short answer on coverage: Our public pen test executive summary (RW-Pentest-Exec-Summary-2025-11.pdf) covers the Redwood-hosted environment only (the Redwood API and control plane hosted by Redwood). It does not include customer Dedicated pools or customer-managed Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.

- Dedicated: we run Dedicated pools in customer VPCs in two models — (1) Redwood-managed Dedicated in a customer VPC (we operate the instances but the compute sits in the customer's cloud project) and (2) fully customer-hosted Dedicated (customer owns the instances and network). Both Dedicated variants are explicitly excluded from the public pen test report.

- Private/VPC/on-prem: Not covered by our public testing. Private deployments are the customer's responsibility; we provide a hardening guide and a partner security checklist.

Details below have the exact wording you can paste into your questionnaire and a small remediation summary for high findings we remediated in 2025. If you need the full test artifacts (raw findings or internal reports) we will need a signed NDA and a short JML (justification + duration) for access — I can route that to our legal team.

Text you can use in your questionnaire:
"Redwood's public penetration test report (RW-Pentest-Exec-Summary-2025-11.pdf) applies to Redwood-hosted API and control plane services maintained by Redwood. Dedicated deployments and customer-managed Private/VPC/on-prem installations are out of scope for that report. For Dedicated or Private assessments, customers can request tailored testing or provide vendor-managed evidence under a mutual NDA and scoped engagement."

Remediation highlights (high findings from 2025 summary):
- Auth bypass vector (CVE-2025-xxxx): mitigated 2025-10-12, verified by internal retest.
- Improper token leakage in logging: mitigated 2025-09-30, logging filters updated; customers can enable additional PII redaction.

I'll attach the executive summary and a remediation tracker CSV with the itemized statuses. CC'ing Dylan and Laura for procurement/contract notes if Acme wants the NDA template or a scoping SOW.

Would you like a short 30-min call early next week to walk through the mapping?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Compliance & Security, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0127

Attachments: RW-Pentest-Exec-Summary-2025-11.pdf; remediation-tracker-20260315.csv

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope clarification for Redwood services

Hi Mina — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

1) For the Dedicated model where Redwood operates instances in a customer VPC (your model (1)), can you confirm whether Redwood's operational access is covered by the public pen test (i.e., did the test consider the operator/admin interfaces used by Redwood engineers when operating Dedicated pools)?

2) For remediation evidence: can you provide dates and artifacts for the retest verification (screenshots, Jira ticket ids, or a short summary per finding)? The tracker CSV is fine but our auditors usually want one piece of evidence per high finding.

We can sign an NDA for the internal artifacts. Please send your NDA template and the SOW/scoping options for Dedicated assessment. Would prefer the NDA by Monday so we can get artifacts next week.

—Rajesh

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope clarification for Redwood services

Rajesh — quick follow-up and next steps so we have a record.

1) Dedicated (Redwood-operated in customer VPC): operator/admin interfaces were included in our internal test cases and the executive summary references operator access controls. That said, because the compute and network belong to the customer account, the public executive summary does not assert coverage of customer-specific networking configurations or customer-managed secrets. For an authoritative statement we will need to run a scoped assessment against the customer’s Dedicated deployment (SOW).

2) Evidence & NDA: attaching our standard Mutual NDA (redwood_nnda_template_2025.pdf) and the remediation tracker (.csv) with one-line evidence columns linking to internal Jira IDs and screenshots stored in our secure evidence repository. Per policy, access to internal artifacts requires a signed NDA plus an access request (email to security-evidence@redwood.com) outlining the JML (what you need and for how long).

Attachments included: RW-Pentest-Exec-Summary-2025-11.pdf; remediation-tracker-20260315.csv; redwood_nnda_template_2025.pdf

If Acme signs the NDA I will coordinate with Security Ops to provision a one-time secure view of the evidence bundle within 3 business days. Also looping Connor for SOW/ops pricing if you want Redwood to run a Dedicated-scoped pen test. Dylan/Laura — can you confirm typical SOW timelines/estimates so I can pass them through?

Proposed next steps (feel free to copy into your tracker):
- Acme signs NDA (we return redlined NDA if necessary) — target: Mon 2026-03-16
- Acme submits access request to security-evidence@redwood.com with JML — target: Tue 2026-03-17
- Redwood Security Ops provisions secure evidence view — ETA: 3 business days after access approved
- Optional: Redwood scoping SOW for Dedicated/PV — Connor to propose timeline & cost by EOD Mon 2026-03-16

Thanks — happy to jump on a call Monday/Tuesday to align.

Best,
Mina
Head of Compliance & Security, Redwood Inference
